findings.text: Two production readers still judge a raw record without the fold this range adds. _record_reads_complete (reckon/crew/review_records.py:630) is reached from _select_stored_record's ranking over records read by _record_file (review_records.py:201), which json.loads the file with no with_canonical_claims; and the classification path that reads a filed record beside an exited run (reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:516) does the same, calling _review_is_complete on a raw json.loads payload at :510. A claims record a reviewer wrote by hand under claim_verdicts therefore still reads incomplete on both, so the added paragraph at docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-only-run-promotes-as-delivered/rorp-s3.html:123-126 asserting that 'every promotion consumer - the classifier, the gate, the obligations pass - asks the same field' overstates the change. The gate and the delivery check are correctly folded; these two ranking and fallback readers are not.

Plan section 3's done_when asks that a claims record missing one claim's verdict be refused 'naming the claim'. The assertion at tests/test_a_claims_review_record_passes_the_check.py:109 accepts the generic 'too few claim verdicts' substring, and the message at reckon/crew/review.py:434 names no rank, so the naming clause is unsatisfied and the gate does not measure it. Carried forward from the prior review of this run; the gained commits do not address it.

The manifest's rubric.evidence line states '73 passed EXIT=0 at the repair head' while its artifacts line and the after_suite log at e064f4e3fc both state 75 passed; the 73 is a stale arm. The same line repeats the earlier round's '45 passed over the four importer files' figure that the prior review found to have no log under the run directory.
